subject: Français (Immersion)
title: Français (Immersion) - Grade 1 French Immersion
description: A comprehensive French language arts program focusing on oral communication, reading, and writing development in an immersion context.
goals: Students will develop foundational French literacy skills through phonological awareness, sight word recognition, guided reading, and emergent writing.
assessmentOverview: Ongoing observation, portfolio assessment, running records, and developmental writing samples.
thematicOverview: French language development through rich thematic units: September - Ma rentrée (Back to School) with classroom routines and greetings; October - Les couleurs de l'automne (Fall Colors) with seasonal vocabulary; November - Ma famille et moi (My Family and Me) exploring relationships; December - Les fêtes et traditions (Holidays and Traditions) with cultural celebrations; January - L'hiver magique (Magical Winter) with weather and activities; February - Les amis et l'amitié (Friends and Friendship) focusing on social connections; March - Le printemps arrive (Spring Arrives) with growth and change; April - Les animaux de notre monde (Animals of Our World) with nature exploration; May - Ma communauté (My Community) with local connections; June - Nos souvenirs et notre avenir (Our Memories and Future) reflecting on learning.
indigenousPerspectives: Authentic integration of Mi'kmaq perspectives throughout French learning: Mi'kmaq place names in Prince Edward Island pronounced and learned alongside French geographical terms; Traditional Mi'kmaq storytelling methods incorporated into French oral traditions, with Elders invited to share stories that connect to our French thematic units; Seasonal teachings aligned with Mi'kmaq understanding of natural cycles while building French vocabulary for weather, animals, and activities; Mi'kmaq family structures and community values explored when learning French family vocabulary, honoring diverse family configurations; Traditional Mi'kmaq games translated into French instruction, supporting physical activity and language learning.
differentiationFramework: {"emergingLearners":"Heavy use of visual supports, gestures, and environmental print; partner support with stronger French speakers; simplified vocabulary and shorter phrases; multisensory learning through movement, music, and art","advancedLearners":"Extension activities with complex French texts; leadership opportunities helping classmates; creative projects requiring higher-order thinking in French; connections to French literature and culture beyond grade level","learningDifferences":"Assistive technology for French language access; alternative communication methods when needed; modified writing expectations with focus on meaning over mechanics; sensory supports for regulation during French instruction","englishLanguageLearners":"Explicit connection between home languages and French; visual vocabulary supports in multiple languages; recognition that multilingual learners have unique strengths; culturally responsive teaching acknowledging diverse backgrounds"}

subject: Mathématiques
title: Mathematics - Grade 1 French Immersion
description: A hands-on mathematics program building number sense, pattern recognition, and spatial reasoning through concrete and visual learning experiences.
goals: Students will develop number sense to 20, understand basic operations, recognize patterns, and explore 2D/3D shapes.
assessmentOverview: Observation during math centers, problem-solving tasks, math journals, and hands-on demonstrations.
thematicOverview: Mathematical thinking development through monthly thematic exploration: September - Collections de la classe (Classroom Collections) exploring sorting, counting, and early number concepts using classroom objects; October - Régularités d'automne (Fall Patterns) discovering patterns in nature, leaves, and seasonal changes while building number sequences; November - Nombres dans notre vie (Numbers in Our Life) investigating how we use numbers at home, school, and in our community; December - Formes et décorations (Shapes and Decorations) exploring 2D and 3D shapes through holiday decorations and winter geometry; January - Mesures et comparaisons (Measurement and Comparisons) using non-standard units to measure classroom objects and comparing lengths, weights; February - Problèmes et solutions (Problems and Solutions) developing problem-solving strategies through real-world mathematical challenges; March - Géométrie dans notre monde (Geometry in Our World) identifying shapes and spatial relationships in architecture and art; April - Données et graphiques (Data and Graphs) collecting, organizing, and representing information about weather, growth, and spring observations; May - Argent et achats (Money and Shopping) exploring Canadian coins and simple transactions; June - Révision mathématique (Mathematical Review) consolidating learning through games, investigations, and mathematical celebrations.
indigenousPerspectives: Respectful integration of Indigenous mathematical traditions: Traditional Mi'kmaq counting systems and number concepts shared alongside French numbers, with attention to cultural protocols and community guidance; Mi'kmaq seasonal calendar and natural patterns explored through mathematical observation and data collection; Traditional games involving mathematical thinking, such as bowl games and counting games, learned with cultural context and respect; Indigenous approaches to spatial reasoning and geometry through traditional art, beadwork patterns, and architectural designs; Mi'kmaq astronomical knowledge connecting to time, measurement, and cyclical thinking; Land-based mathematics learning from traditional ecological knowledge about animal populations, plant cycles, and resource management.
differentiationFramework: {"additionalSupport":"Extended time with concrete manipulatives before moving to abstract concepts; visual supports and graphic organizers for problem-solving; simplified mathematical language with key vocabulary emphasis","advancedStudents":"Open-ended problems with multiple solution paths; opportunities to explain mathematical thinking to peers; extension activities involving higher-order mathematical concepts","englishLanguageLearners":"Mathematical instruction leveraging universal mathematical concepts; visual and hands-on approaches reducing language barriers; peer translation support when appropriate","learningDifferences":"Assistive technology for mathematical access; alternative assessment methods showing mathematical understanding; modified mathematical expectations aligned with individual learning goals"}

subject: Sciences de la nature
title: Natural Sciences - Grade 1 French Immersion
titleFr: Sciences de la nature - 1re année immersion
description: An inquiry-based science program exploring living things, energy, and seasonal changes through hands-on investigations.
goals: Students will observe and classify living things, explore energy uses, and understand seasonal patterns and their effects.
assessmentOverview: Science journals, observational drawings, simple experiments, and oral explanations of findings.
thematicOverview: Seasonal inquiry-based exploration of natural world: September - Découverte de notre cour d'école (Discovering Our Schoolyard) through nature walks, observation journals, and collection of natural specimens; October - Changements d'automne (Fall Changes) investigating leaf transformations, animal preparations for winter, and seasonal weather patterns; November - Caractéristiques des êtres vivants (Characteristics of Living Things) exploring what makes something alive through plant and animal observations; December - Adaptation en hiver (Winter Adaptations) studying how plants and animals survive cold weather; January - Sources d'énergie autour de nous (Energy Sources Around Us) discovering how we use energy for heat, light, and movement; February - Cycle de l'eau en hiver (Winter Water Cycle) observing ice, snow, and water transformations; March - Signes du printemps (Signs of Spring) documenting emerging plants, returning animals, and changing daylight; April - Jardinage et croissance (Gardening and Growth) planting seeds and observing life cycles; May - Écosystème de notre communauté (Our Community Ecosystem) exploring local habitats and animal homes; June - Bilan scientifique (Scientific Summary) reflecting on seasonal observations and planning summer investigations.
indigenousPerspectives: Mi'kmaq ecological knowledge integrated throughout scientific learning: Traditional Mi'kmaq understanding of seasonal cycles and natural indicators, shared with cultural protocols and community partnership; Mi'kmaq plant knowledge including traditional uses, sustainable harvesting practices, and medicinal applications appropriate for young learners; Animal relationships and traditional ecological knowledge about local wildlife behavior, migration patterns, and habitat needs; Mi'kmaq astronomy and connection to natural cycles, seasonal stars, and traditional calendar keeping; Water teachings and understanding of sacred relationships with rivers, lakes, and ocean systems; Traditional weather prediction methods and observation of natural signs for seasonal changes.
differentiationFramework: {"emergingScientists":"Concrete hands-on experiences before abstract concepts; visual supports and graphic organizers for scientific thinking; simplified scientific language with key vocabulary emphasis","advancedLearners":"Open-ended investigations with multiple variables; opportunities to design their own scientific experiments; connections to more complex scientific concepts","learningDifferences":"Multi-sensory scientific experiences addressing different learning styles; assistive technology for scientific documentation; alternative methods for showing scientific understanding","englishLanguageLearners":"Scientific learning leveraging universal observation and investigation; visual and hands-on approaches reducing language barriers"}

subject: Sciences humaines
title: Social Studies - Grade 1 French Immersion
description: A community-centered program exploring identity, citizenship, geography, and relationships in family, school, and community contexts.
goals: Students will understand their roles and responsibilities, appreciate diversity, develop mapping skills, and explore needs vs wants.
assessmentOverview: Community projects, family presentations, map creation, role-playing activities, and class discussions.
thematicOverview: Community and identity exploration throughout the year: September - Qui suis-je? (Who Am I?) exploring individual identity, family backgrounds, and personal strengths; October - Ma famille unique (My Unique Family) celebrating diverse family structures, traditions, and cultural backgrounds; November - Notre classe comme communauté (Our Classroom Community) building classroom citizenship, rights, responsibilities, and collaborative decision-making; December - Traditions et célébrations (Traditions and Celebrations) exploring cultural traditions, holiday celebrations, and family customs from diverse backgrounds; January - Notre école et ses règles (Our School and Its Rules) understanding school community, rules, roles, and democratic participation; February - Amitié et résolution de conflits (Friendship and Conflict Resolution) developing social skills, empathy, and peaceful problem-solving strategies; March - Ma communauté locale (My Local Community) exploring neighborhood, local businesses, community helpers, and civic engagement; April - Les cartes et notre monde (Maps and Our World) developing geographic skills, understanding directions, and exploring local and global connections; May - Besoins et désirs (Needs and Wants) understanding economic concepts, making choices, and appreciating resources; June - Être un bon citoyen (Being a Good Citizen) reflecting on community contributions, environmental stewardship, and future aspirations.
indigenousPerspectives: Authentic integration of Mi'kmaq history, culture, and ongoing presence: Recognition of Mi'kmaq as the first peoples of Prince Edward Island, with age-appropriate understanding of traditional territories and ongoing stewardship; Mi'kmaq family structures and community values explored alongside diverse modern family configurations; Traditional Mi'kmaq governance and decision-making processes introduced as examples of democratic participation and community care; Mi'kmaq place names and their meanings connecting to geographic learning and cultural understanding; Traditional Mi'kmaq seasonal round and connection to land, resources, and sustainable living practices; Seven Sacred Teachings integrated into character education and social skills development; Contemporary Mi'kmaq communities and contributions to PEI society, including artists, leaders, and knowledge keepers.
differentiationFramework: {"shyStudents":"Multiple ways to participate in social activities including drawing, writing, or small group sharing; respect for different comfort levels with public speaking","socialChallenges":"Explicit teaching of social skills with visual supports and practice opportunities; structured social interactions with clear expectations","englishLanguageLearners":"Social learning leveraging non-verbal communication and universal concepts; peer translation and cultural bridge-building when appropriate","diverseBackgrounds":"Affirmation and celebration of all family structures, cultural practices, and traditions; anti-bias education addressing stereotypes and promoting inclusion"}

subject: Arts visuels
title: Visual Arts - Grade 1 French Immersion
description: A creative arts program developing artistic expression, technique exploration, and cultural appreciation through hands-on art making.
goals: Students will explore various art materials and techniques, express ideas through art, and appreciate art in their culture.
assessmentOverview: Portfolio development, artist statements, peer feedback, and process observations.
thematicOverview: Process-focused artistic exploration celebrating creativity: September - Couleurs et émotions (Colors and Emotions) exploring color theory through personal expression and feeling exploration; October - Art dans la nature (Art in Nature) using natural materials for creative expression and environmental art projects; November - Portraits et identité (Portraits and Identity) celebrating individual uniqueness through self-portraits and family representations; December - Art et traditions (Art and Traditions) creating artwork inspired by diverse cultural traditions and holiday celebrations; January - Formes et sculptures (Shapes and Sculptures) exploring 3D art, clay work, and sculptural expression; February - Art communautaire (Community Art) collaborating on large-scale projects and appreciating local artists; March - Printemps créatif (Creative Spring) nature-inspired art connecting to seasonal observations and growth; April - Histoires visuelles (Visual Stories) creating narrative art and illustrated stories; May - Art et techniques (Art and Techniques) exploring various artistic methods, tools, and media; June - Galerie et célébration (Gallery and Celebration) curating student artwork and reflecting on artistic growth.
indigenousPerspectives: Respectful integration of Mi'kmaq artistic traditions: Traditional Mi'kmaq art forms including beadwork, basket making, and quillwork introduced with cultural protocols and community partnership; Mi'kmaq symbols and their meanings explored with respect and proper cultural context; Traditional colors and materials used in Mi'kmaq art, with understanding of cultural significance; Mi'kmaq pottery and sculpture traditions connecting to 3D art explorations; Traditional Mi'kmaq storytelling through visual art and pictographs; Connection to contemporary Mi'kmaq artists and their contributions to Canadian art; Seasonal art projects reflecting Mi'kmaq understanding of natural cycles and relationships.
differentiationFramework: {"fineMotorSupport":"Adapted art tools and materials for easier manipulation; extended time for artistic creation and detailed work","artisticallyAdvanced":"Access to more complex art materials and techniques; leadership opportunities in peer teaching and collaboration","sensoryDifferences":"Sensory-friendly art materials and alternatives for different sensitivities; quiet spaces for artistic creation when needed","englishLanguageLearners":"Artistic expression as universal language transcending verbal communication; visual vocabulary development through art making"}

subject: Formation personnelle et sociale
title: Personal and Social Development - Grade 1 French Immersion
titleFr: Formation personnelle et sociale - 1re année immersion
description: A comprehensive wellness program focusing on personal health, safety, relationships, and self-awareness.
goals: Students will develop healthy habits, understand safety practices, build positive relationships, and recognize their strengths.
assessmentOverview: Self-reflections, safety demonstrations, social scenarios, and health habit tracking.
thematicOverview: Social-emotional learning integrated throughout daily experiences: September - Se connaître soi-même (Getting to Know Myself) exploring personal identity, strengths, and uniqueness; October - Émotions et sentiments (Emotions and Feelings) developing emotional vocabulary and regulation strategies; November - Relations familiales (Family Relationships) appreciating family diversity and building family connections; December - Gratitude et générosité (Gratitude and Generosity) developing appreciation and giving spirit during holiday season; January - Objectifs et résolutions (Goals and Resolutions) setting personal goals and developing growth mindset; February - Amitié et empathie (Friendship and Empathy) building social skills and understanding others' perspectives; March - Sécurité et bien-être (Safety and Wellness) learning personal safety and wellness strategies; April - Résolution de conflits (Conflict Resolution) developing peaceful problem-solving skills; May - Responsabilité et leadership (Responsibility and Leadership) exploring personal and community responsibility; June - Croissance et avenir (Growth and Future) reflecting on personal development and planning ahead.
indigenousPerspectives: Seven Sacred Teachings integrated into character development: WISDOM (Nibwaakaawin) - Cherishing knowledge and understanding, seeking guidance from Elders and teachers, appreciating traditional knowledge alongside contemporary learning. LOVE (Zaagi'idiwin) - Developing unconditional love for family, community, and all living things; showing care and compassion in daily interactions. RESPECT (Mnaadendimowin) - Honoring all people, cultures, and living beings; showing respect for differences and diverse ways of being; respecting traditional territories and cultural protocols. TRUTH (Debwewin) - Being honest in words and actions; understanding the importance of truthfulness in relationships; speaking and living authentically. HUMILITY (Dibaadendizwin) - Recognizing individual place in the larger community; appreciating others' gifts and contributions; understanding interconnectedness with all life. BRAVERY (Aakwe'ewin) - Courage to do what is right even when difficult; facing challenges with inner strength; standing up for others and for justice. HONESTY (Gwekwaadiziwin) - Living with integrity and authenticity; being truthful with self and others; honoring commitments and responsibilities.
differentiationFramework: {"socialEmotionalChallenges":"Individualized behavior plans with positive reinforcement; additional support for emotional regulation and social skills","traumaExperiences":"Trauma-informed approaches to social-emotional learning; recognition of individual triggers and support needs","autismDifferences":"Visual supports and structured social learning opportunities; explicit teaching of social norms and expectations","englishLanguageLearners":"Social-emotional learning that transcends language barriers; peer support and buddy systems","anxietyNeeds":"Modified expectations for social participation; additional supports for emotional regulation"}

subject: Éducation physique
title: Physical Education - Grade 1 French Immersion
description: A developmental PE program building fundamental movement skills, cooperation, and healthy active living habits.
goals: Students will master basic locomotor and manipulative skills, work cooperatively, and understand the importance of physical activity.
assessmentOverview: Movement skill checklists, peer cooperation rubrics, self-assessments, and participation observations.
thematicOverview: Fundamental movement development through inclusive physical activity: Fall - Locomotor skill development including walking, running, jumping, hopping, and skipping with proper form and safety; spatial awareness activities and movement in personal and general space; cooperative games building teamwork and inclusive participation. Winter - Manipulative skills including throwing, catching, kicking, and striking using various equipment; hand-eye and foot-eye coordination development; introduction to simple games and modified sports activities. Spring - Balance, stability, and gymnastics movements including rolling, weight transfer, and basic sequences; outdoor activities and nature-based movement; culminating physical literacy celebrations and demonstrations.
indigenousPerspectives: Traditional Indigenous games and physical activities: Integration of traditional Mi'kmaq games when culturally appropriate; understanding of Indigenous approaches to physical activity and community sport; respect for land-based physical activities and outdoor education; incorporation of traditional teamwork and cooperation values.
differentiationFramework: {"adaptivePhysEd":"Modified equipment and activities for different ability levels; alternative ways to participate and demonstrate physical literacy","inclusiveGames":"Peer support systems and inclusive game modifications; celebration of individual progress and effort","healthNeeds":"Collaboration with families and support professionals for students with physical or health needs"}

subject: Music
title: Music - Grade 1
description: An exploratory music program developing musical literacy, performance skills, and cultural appreciation through active music-making.
goals: Students will create music, develop performance skills, understand musical elements, and appreciate diverse musical styles.
assessmentOverview: Performance assessments, creative compositions, listening reflections, and participation in musical activities.
thematicOverview: Musical exploration through creative expression and cultural appreciation: Fall - Sound exploration and rhythm development through body percussion and simple instruments; singing games and folk songs from diverse cultures; introduction to musical concepts of loud/soft and fast/slow. Winter - Melody and singing development with simple songs and vocal play; instrument exploration including classroom percussion; creative movement and dance to various musical styles. Spring - Musical creativity through composition and improvisation; performance preparation and sharing; appreciation of diverse musical traditions and community musicians.
indigenousPerspectives: Integration of Indigenous musical traditions: Exposure to Mi'kmaq traditional songs and instruments when culturally appropriate; understanding of music as cultural expression and storytelling; respect for Indigenous approaches to musical education and community celebration.
differentiationFramework: {"adaptiveInstruments":"Adaptive instruments and alternative participation methods","visualKinesthetic":"Visual and kinesthetic approaches to musical learning","comfortLevels":"Respect for different comfort levels with singing and performance","diverseBackgrounds":"Celebration of diverse musical backgrounds and cultural traditions","hearingDifferences":"Support for students with hearing differences or other special needs"}
